scope: Untimed Standard best-of-three coordination in the shared Rust engine and JSON bot API, with fixed registrations, sideboarding, private battlefield commitments, play order, ordered mulligans, completed-game scoring, concessions and intentional draws.

rust.scope: All 106 Cargo all-targets test harnesses, run with eight independent workers

focused_rust.scope: Matches run to actual engine winners. Irelia swaps Edge of Night for Ravenbloom Prefect before game two; Master Yi and Rengar use explicit legal empty-sideboard registrations, not invented tournament sideboards. Focused reruns are not counted as extra distinct games.

python.scope: Full existing tools source-check suite; no added Python unit tests. The new example is exercised by the release API campaign.

api.scope: Twelve complete API-driven Arito mirror matches, three levels, both designated seats and both first-player choices. Each seat swaps one Edge of Night for Ravenbloom Prefect before game two; no draw or concession is substituted for completing games.

release.source_note: All source, test, tool and asset bytes match the frozen inputs used for the full suites and release/API runs. Documentation and this receipt were completed after those runs.

rules_review.method: The current official Rules Hub and October tournament changelog were browsed. The linked official Tournament Rules PDF was downloaded, text-extracted and selected pages visually reviewed; the previously accepted October 9 Core Rules were reread for setup and match references.
findings: Tournament registrations require exactly forty main cards including the chosen champion, up to ten sideboard cards, twelve runes and three differently named legal battlefields.

Named-card limits cover the main and sideboard together. Between games, main and side exchange one for one; the registered legend, runes and battlefield set cannot change. Chosen champions may change to eligible cards in the resulting main deck.
Both battlefield choices remain private until committed. Play order is chosen before opening hands and mulligans proceed in turn order.
A decisive game retires both revealed battlefields. The previous loser chooses the next starting player. Two game wins finish the match.
A drawn game preserves the deck configurations, fields and starting player, gives no game win and opens no sideboarding window.
The agreed random method or playoff ranking supplies the first designated player to the host. Reproducible shuffling seeds do not substitute for that choice.
Event-specific opening-rule trials do not replace the current published Standard opening.

behavior_checks: Illegal registration, stale revision, outside-pool swaps, illegal copy counts, unavailable cards, changed immutable fields and wrong-phase requests are rejected without changing either player observation.
Opponent card pools, sideboards and unrevealed field choices remain private. New chosen champions reveal only after both sideboard submissions.
Game actions cannot run during sideboarding or setup, and old game hands are absent from those observations. Registered matches require explicit mulligans from both seats in turn order.
Concessions before field reveal do not expose or retire a private choice. Match concessions and draws do not fabricate individual game wins.
Mutually accepted game draws begin fresh shuffles and mulligans with the retained setup. Successful game actions clear pending draw offers.
Standalone reset removes the series and retains the previous individual-game protocol behavior.
findings_resolved: Initial compilation required an explicit Vec type on the collected sideboard remainder. All successful build and test evidence follows this correction.
limitations: The native app still runs individual games. Its match setup, between-game sideboarding and match-results screens are not integrated or visually tested by this update.
Only sourced preset 5 includes a complete runtime match registration. Other presets require explicitly supplied legal registrations.
Timed tournament rounds, end-of-time procedures, judge penalties, best-of-five and game-draw requests before setup remain unfinished.
The example bot keeps its sideboard by default. Scripted test swaps are not evidence of advanced matchup strategy or expert-strength AI.
Supported card coverage and remaining in-game fidelity limits are unchanged. This update does not establish complete Standard rules parity or individual combat damage attribution.
The accepted catalog remains dated; no fresh full-gallery acceptance is claimed.
The local coordinator is trusted to route observations and player actions. This is not an authenticated multiplayer server.
Acceptance was on x86-64 Linux. No new independent Nix validation was run; the last separately validated Nix source remains commit 6411bd141a3bff35eb6491e2a6202496045030bf.
